neighbours.label: a common head noun (program, story, study, states, site, project) right after a name or noun that says WHICH one ('the Botswana program', 'the rabbit story', 'McCain states'); the same nouns with only an article or a plain adjective stay low
fire: Funding for the Malawi program was renewed for another three years.
My grandmother knew two endings to the coyote story and told both.
Turnout rose sharply in the Reagan states that year.
Critics pointed out several flaws in the Stanford study last month.
Volunteers post weekly updates on the Greenpeace site for supporters.
Engineers spent a decade on the Hubble project before launch.
Children in the village still act out the spider story every autumn.
After the pilot, the Uganda program was extended to forty more clinics.
quiet: Funding for the program was renewed for another three years.
My grandmother knew two endings to that story and told both.

notes: Card: no single token (' site', ' story', ' states', ' program', '_port', ' guns'), each a generic noun right after a specifying modifier (Dreaming site, 'trouble' story, McCain states, Botswana program, or_port, crime guns). Probes: rabbit story 0.59, Botswana program 0.52, Kerry states 0.50, Harvard study 0.38, Dreaming site 0.33; bare 'The program' 0.03, 'a story' 0.08; weaker when two such phrases share a sentence (0.18) and for 'crime guns' (0.16). The - pole fires on the generic part of place names (Richardson Bay, Lapham Peak): a proper-name head instead of a common-noun head.
